{
    "improvements": [
        {
            "id": "IMP-001",
            "description": "Define key bootstrap and distribution procedure for new operators/machines, including how the maintainer offline root key is initially generated, escrowed, and recovered if the maintainer becomes unavailable.",
            "rationale": "Section 1.9.3.1 requires every audit log to verify against the trust-store signed by an offline root key, but provides no bus-factor mitigation. If the maintainer loses the root key or is unavailable, no trust-store updates are possible and key rotation halts indefinitely. This is a single point of failure for the entire signing scheme.",
            "location": "Section 1.9.3.1 (Trust-store root of trust)",
            "priority": "HIGH",
            "confidence": 0.85
        },
        {
            "id": "IMP-002",
            "description": "Specify the exact byte-level canonicalization input for `prev_hash` and signature computation (field ordering, payload nesting, Unicode normalization, number representation) and provide a worked example with hex bytes alongside the conformance vectors.",
            "rationale": "Section 3.2.1 describes prev_hash as 'SHA-256 of canonical-JSON of prior entry's content (excluding signature + signing_key_id)' but this still leaves ambiguity about whether `redaction_applied: null` is included, how floating-point payload numbers are serialized under JCS, and whether nested payload sub-objects are recursively canonicalized. Cross-implementation hash drift will silently break chains. A worked example with bytes is the only unambiguous spec.",
            "location": "Section 3.2.1, Section 5.2.1",
            "priority": "HIGH",
            "confidence": 0.9
        },
        {
            "id": "IMP-003",
            "description": "Add explicit threat model for the machine-fingerprint check, including what attack it does and does not prevent (e.g., it does not prevent a single-machine attacker with filesystem access from forging entries; an operator who copies `.run/machine-fingerprint` along with audit logs bypasses the check).",
            "rationale": "Section 1.7.1 introduces fingerprint guardrails as a 'hard runtime guardrail' but the fingerprint file is itself untracked and unsigned. An operator copying the entire `.run/` directory to a second machine bypasses the check trivially. The SDD presents this as a security boundary when it is really a foot-gun preventer. Mis-stating the threat model invites over-reliance.",
            "location": "Section 1.7.1 (Hard Runtime Guardrails)",
            "priority": "HIGH",
            "confidence": 0.85
        },
        {
            "id": "IMP-004",
            "description": "Specify concrete latency/SLO measurement methodology and CI gating thresholds for write-path SLOs (audit log append p95 <50ms, p99 <200ms) — including measurement environment, sample size, what counts as a 'write', and what happens when CI exceeds threshold.",
            "rationale": "The v1.2 changelog cites IMP-005 as adding 'latency/SLO targets for write path' but the body only mentions them in passing. Without measurement methodology (cold vs warm cache, with/without flock contention, signing key cache state), the SLO is unenforceable. Ed25519 signing + ajv validation + flock + jq canonical-JSON + git history check on every append is a non-trivial budget for 50ms p95.",
            "rationale_ext": "",
            "location": "Section 6.4 / Section 7.1",
            "priority": "MEDIUM",
            "confidence": 0.8
        },
        {
            "id": "IMP-005",
            "description": "Define the tool-resolver provenance-tagging mechanism concretely: where `provenance: untrusted-session-start` metadata is stored, how the tool resolver introspects it, and what 'first N turns' means operationally. Provide an enforcement test case.",
            "rationale": "Section 1.9.3.2 Layer 5 describes deny-by-default tool resolution as the load-bearing security boundary, but the implementation is vague ('heuristic: any tool call within first N turns'). N is not defined; persistence of the provenance tag across context compaction is not specified; integration with Loa's existing tool-call harness is not described. Without a concrete mechanism this is aspirational, not implemented.",
            "location": "Section 1.9.3.2 (Layer 5 — Hard tool-call boundary)",
            "priority": "HIGH",
            "confidence": 0.85
        },
        {
            "id": "IMP-006",
            "description": "Add explicit specification for L2 cost-budget behavior when multiple cycles run concurrently on the same machine (e.g., L3 nightly cron + interactive operator session). Define whether the counter is per-process, shared via flock, and how race conditions on the warn-90/halt-100 threshold are resolved.",
            "rationale": "Section 1.4.2 L2 describes per-cycle and per-session tracking but the system explicitly supports concurrent L3 schedules and operator sessions. Two near-simultaneous paid calls each reading 89% usage could both decide 'allow' and push the day over 100%. The fail-closed guarantee (G-2) is undermined without a documented locking discipline on the counter.",
            "location": "Section 1.4.2 (L2), Section 5.4",
            "priority": "HIGH",
            "confidence": 0.85
        },
        {
            "id": "IMP-007",
            "description": "Specify the per-event-type payload schema registry mechanism: where schemas live, naming convention, validation gate (CI vs runtime), version evolution rules, and what happens when an unknown event_type is encountered on read.",
            "rationale": "v1.1 changelog cites IMP-001 'per-event-type payload schemas + schema registry pattern + CI validation step' but Section 3.2 only enumerates event_type examples. There is no schema for any specific event_type body, no registry path stated, and no read-side handling for unknown types. This is the crux of long-term schema evolution and is currently unresolved despite being marked integrated.",
            "location": "Section 3.2, Section 5.2",
            "priority": "MEDIUM",
            "confidence": 0.85
        },
        {
            "id": "IMP-008",
            "description": "Provide a concrete L4 trust ledger merge/conflict resolution algorithm for the documented divergent-valid-chains case, including the merge marker injection format, the operator arbitration UI, and how chain integrity is restored post-merge.",
            "rationale": "v1.2 changelog cites IMP-003 'git-backed conflict resolution protocol for divergent valid chains' as integrated, but Section 3.4 does not contain this protocol — only the §3.4.4 hash-chain recovery for tampering. The trust ledger is the one tracked-in-git audit log, so git merge conflicts are the most likely real-world failure mode and need explicit handling.",
            "location": "Section 3.4 (Migration Strategy)",
            "priority": "MEDIUM",
            "confidence": 0.85
        },
        {
            "id": "IMP-009",
            "description": "Replace `jq -S -c` references in the glossary and Section 2.2 with consistent RFC 8785 JCS terminology, since the v1.2 SKP-004 explicitly removes `jq -S -c` as a canonicalization mechanism but the body and appendix still reference it.",
            "rationale": "v1.2 changelog states 'Removes jq -S -c references' and 'Mixed-mode verification rejected', but Section 2.2 still lists 'Canonical JSON via jq -S -c' as a backend technology, Appendix A glossary defines canonical-JSON as 'Computed via jq -S -c', and the bats test in Section 7.2.1 uses `jq -S -c` to compute hash. This contradiction will cause implementer confusion and the conformance vectors will not match.",
            "location": "Section 2.2, Section 7.2.1, Appendix A",
            "priority": "HIGH",
            "confidence": 0.95
        },
        {
            "id": "IMP-010",
            "description": "Add an integration test specification (or explicit deferral) for the maintainer offline-root-key signing workflow, including how the test exercises the offline ceremony without exposing real keys, and how CI verifies the pinned root pubkey integrity check.",
            "rationale": "Section 1.9.3.1 makes the offline root key the foundation of trust, with documented failure modes including 'all audit log verifications fail' on tampering. Yet Section 7 testing strategy contains no test for this critical path. Untested security ceremonies historically break silently. Either specify the test or explicitly defer with rationale.",
            "location": "Section 7 (Testing Strategy)",
            "priority": "MEDIUM",
            "confidence": 0.8
        }
    ],
    "summary": "10 improvements identified, 6 HIGH priority, 4 MEDIUM priority. Key themes: ambiguity in cryptographic canonicalization (IMP-002, IMP-009), unresolved security mechanism details (IMP-003, IMP-005, IMP-001), concurrency/integrity gaps (IMP-006, IMP-008), and integration deltas where v1.1/v1.2 changelog claims are not fully reflected in the body (IMP-007, IMP-008, IMP-009)."
}
